diagnosis: Supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous return
symptom: a child who got tired and breathless while playing
hook: the heart looked exactly like a snowman
whatYouSee: The heart and a widened upper mediastinum make a figure of 8 like a snowman with busy lung vessels.
whyItMatters: In supracardiac TAPVR all four pulmonary veins drain into a vertical vein that empties into the innominate vein and the superior vena cava. The dilated veins form the snowman head. Survival depends on an atrial septal defect that lets mixed blood reach the left heart.
treatment: Treatment is surgery to reconnect the pulmonary veins to the left atrium. Obstructed forms are a neonatal emergency.
takeaway: A snowman heart on a chest X-ray is supracardiac TAPVR.
igOptions: A. Supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous return
B. Transposition of the great arteries

observations.observed: The anatomy is a chest with symmetric ribs, one clavicle and one scapula per side, a single cardiac silhouette and one hemidiaphragm per side. The proportions are pediatric. There is no lettering and no duplicated anatomy.

findings: Frontal (AP or PA) chest radiograph of a small/pediatric-appearing patient, with the arms at the sides and the upper abdomen included.
Marked cardiomegaly with a large globular cardiac silhouette that extends to both sides of the spine and fills much of the mid and lower chest.

A separate rounded or bulbous soft-tissue opacity in the superior mediastinum above the cardiac silhouette, creating a figure-of-eight or snowman contour. It is wide and extends laterally on both sides.
The lungs are relatively clear and hyperlucent, with fine, delicate vascular markings. There is no focal consolidation, large effusion or pneumothorax.
The lung vascularity looks normal or slightly diminished, with no obvious pulmonary edema.
Both hemidiaphragms are smooth. A large soft-tissue density in the right upper abdomen is consistent with the liver. Bowel gas is present in the left abdomen.
The visible ribs and clavicles are symmetric, and the spine is not clearly abnormal. The image is slightly rotated or tilted.
differential: Congenital heart disease with a snowman-type silhouette, such as supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous return, with marked cardiomegaly
Large pericardial effusion or cardiomyopathy with a prominent superior mediastinal vascular shadow
Mediastinal mass, such as a thymic mass or lymphoma, superimposed on cardiomegaly
anatomyConcerns: No impossible anatomy is identified. The figure-of-eight mediastinal contour is plausible as pathology and is not an acquisition artifact.
Slight rotation or tilt of the image and a cropped lower edge. The thymus cannot be separated from the vascular pedicle.
The projection (AP vs PA) is uncertain, which can exaggerate the cardiac size.

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The film shows a classic figure-of-8 snowman contour. A large globular enlarged heart forms the lower round part, and a wide, smooth, bulbous superior mediastinum extending to both sides forms the upper part. In a child with exertional fatigue and breathlessness, this pattern best fits supracardiac TAPVR. The alternatives are a thymic mass or a pericardial effusion, but a symmetric, smooth supracardiac pedicle with cardiomegaly favors the vertical vein, innominate vein and SVC configuration. The limits are that the lungs look relatively clear and hyperlucent rather than plethoric, and an AP projection cannot be excluded. The slight rotation and cropping are acquisition features. The ribs, clavicles and spine are symmetric, with no extra or fused structures, and the child's skeletal proportions are appropriate. No lettering or side marker is visible.

clueFacts.fact: In supracardiac TAPVR all pulmonary venous blood returns to the right heart so the lungs are flooded with extra blood flow, which typically causes breathlessness on exertion such as play.
Tiredness every time a child played fits TAPVR because only mixed blood crosses the atrial septal defect from right to left to reach the left heart, so oxygen delivery falls on exertion.
